# Signatories
<!--
This section provides the ISC with a view of the support received from
the community for a proposal. Acceptance isn't predicated on
popularity but community acceptance is important. Willingness to
accept outside input is also a good marker for project delivery.

An optional section would be for R-Core signatories where changes to R
are proposed.
-->

## Project team
<!--
Who are the people responsible for actually delivering the project if
the proposal gets accepted and are already signed up and rearing to
go? Briefly describe all participants and the skills they will bring
to the project.
-->

**Daniel Rakotomalala** (proposer, sole developer). Author and
maintainer of `genproc` and of `scrutr` (data validation), both on
CRAN, and of `cryptRopen` (dataset pseudonymisation, on GitHub). PhD in
economics. Data scientist and project lead in a national statistical
service, where the pipelines that motivated `genproc` run daily.
Skills: R package development (S3, non-standard evaluation, AST
rewriting), the `future` ecosystem, CI/CD, technical writing. GitHub:
<https://github.com/danielrak>; project site:
<https://danielrak.github.io/genproc/>. He works on `genproc` outside
a full-time job; the 260 hours below are about five hours a week.

The proposer uses AI coding assistants (large language models) to draft
code, tests and text, including parts of this document. He designs,
reviews every change, tests the package by hand and takes every
decision; the code is kept readable so that it can be maintained
without such tools.

## Contributors
<!--
Who are the people who have actively helped with this proposal but
won't necessarily be on the core project team later?
-->

None at submission; the work is sized for one developer. Contributors
will be invited from Milestone 1 (contract review) and Milestone 4
(evaluation).

## Consulted
<!--
Who has been given the opportunity to provide feedback on the
proposal? This should include any R Consortium & ISC members who the
proposal has been discussed with.
-->

- **Henrik Bengtsson**, author of `future`, `future.apply` and
  `progressr`, on which the parallel, non-blocking and monitoring layers
  are built, and the R Foundation's representative on the ISC.
  Contacted in April 2026; he replied in detail. On the whole, he saw
  these topics as ones the R community would benefit from
  standardising, for sequential as well as parallel processing. Three
  specific points shaped this proposal: define the retry rules for
  sequential processing first, then carry them to parallel processing;
  use `progressr` conditions for monitoring (done in 0.2.0) and extend
  them to non-blocking runs (Milestone 3); stay above `future::plan()`
  and leave backend negotiation to the futureverse.
- **William Michael Landau**, author of `targets`. Contacted in April
  2026 on the positioning of `genproc` relative to `targets`. No reply
  at the time of writing.

No other ISC member has been consulted. Feedback from R users in
public statistics and clinical data will be sought in the start-up
phase.
